narration.text: You shipped something. You need a video, and it costs you a day.
Other tools record clicks and hand you an mp4 you can't edit. LaunchReel reads a terminal session instead.
Point it at a recording — asciinema or vhs.
It ingests the cast: dimensions, every command, every output.
It measures each line of narration and stretches the shot to fit.
What comes out is a structured project file, not a stitched screencast.
The build ships with seventy-three passing tests.
But the hard part is the music.
Three candidates, measured with librosa. The track whose beats actually land on the cuts wins.
Narration: synthesize, measure, then fix the timeline to the audio that came out.
When a beat is found, the cut is marked on it.
It opens in a real editor as FCPXML.
You get two things, not one.
A finished mp4. And the project file — cuts on the beats.
One command. One video. One editable timeline.
It ships with a recorded session. No API key, no network, no Python. Free and open source, MIT.
